newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy targets 2.8 pct deficit-GDP ratio for 1998.
newsitem.headline: Italy targets 2.8 pct deficit-GDP ratio for 1998.

text.p: Italy's centre-left government has set a target deficit-to-GDP ratio of 2.8 percent for 1998, a labour union source said on Wednesday.

The objective, to be contained in a document of three-year rolling economic targets expected to be approved by the cabinet on Friday, is tighter than the 3.0 percent target for 1998 set in last year's document, known as the DPEF. Countries wishing to join Europe's single currency must keep their deficit-GDP ratio at 3.0 percent or below.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi has said he is confident that the 1997 budget deficit will hit the target for economic and monetary union (EMU) after his government drew up a supplementary budget to try to wipe out a deficit overshoot.
The labour union source, who requested anonymity, was speaking to Reuters after Prodi met leaders of Italy's three main labour confederations on Tuesday night to discuss the forthcoming DPEF.

The deficit-GDP ratio for 1998 is based on expected budget deficit cuts of 25 trillion lire. The union source said government plans on control of pension spending included an objective that the bill should not grow faster than GDP.

Union leaders have warned they cannot accept unlimited welfare cuts to meet the deficit goal and the hard-left Communist Refoundation party, whose support secures Prodi's parliamentary majority, is opposed to any cuts in social spending.
